title: A dusty spiral in Virgo
caption: The edge-on spiral galaxy NGC 4206, imaged by the Hubble Space Telescope
celestial: NGC 4206 · constellation Virgo · about 70 million light-years away (source figure)

recognition.text: ESA/Hubble Picture of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: Vast streaks of dust run along this edge-on spiral galaxy, partly veiling the bulge at its centre, which is only just visible. Near the edges, scattered clumps that appear blue mark places where new stars are being born. This is NGC 4206, about 70 million light-years away in the constellation Virgo.
The bulge tells a different story from the edges. It is mostly made of older, redder stars, and very little star formation happens there.

Hubble took this image as part of a snapshot survey of nearby edge-on spirals. The goal was to measure how the material between stars, the interstellar medium, affects light passing through it. The Advanced Camera for Surveys can reveal the dust and hydrogen gas in the cold parts of that medium. Astronomers then map how the material absorbs and scatters light, an effect called extinction, which makes objects look redder to us.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (3.45 x 2.78 arcminutes) and distance (70 million light years), the frame spans roughly 70,000 × 57,000 light-years. Its light set out about 70 million years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: This image comes from Hubble's Advanced Camera for Surveys and combines visible and near-infrared filters. The caption notes that star-forming clumps appear blue, but the filter-to-colour mapping is not published.
understand.eye: The galaxy can be seen with moderate amateur telescopes, but not in this detail, and part of the data is near-infrared light that the eye cannot detect.

explore: NGC 4206 shines at 13th magnitude and can be seen with most moderate amateur telescopes. William Herschel discovered it on 17 April 1784. Contestant Nick Rose submitted a version of this picture to Hubble's Hidden Treasures competition.
alt: An edge-on spiral galaxy crossed by vast streaks of dust that partly hide its central bulge, with blue clumps toward its edges.
